extracted.intended_audience: educated readers and writers (essayists) interested in conduct, rhetoric, and literary style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing personal, reflective essays and for comportment in matters of love and social behavior; mixes stylistic rules for prose with practical maxims about courtship, modesty, and jealousy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing in matters of love
rubrics_metrics.description: The first, second, and third thing to be considered in love matters is how to take a fitting time; 'tis a point that can do everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunity is a furious advantage; one may sometimes lack fortune or fail oneself in attempt. Choosing the right moment is crucial for success in courtship and amorous enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverence and modesty in courtship
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a great respect for the loved one; preserve reverence because he who in this traffic takes away the reverence defaces the lustre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A man should at times play the child, the timorous, and the servant—bashfulness and modesty increase attraction; losing reverence harms the relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false professions of chastity and affected looks
rubrics_metrics.description: When persons boast of coldness and insensibility in love with a serious countenance, affected looks and eyes that belie the tongue make the claim ridiculous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected dissimulation invites ridicule; conceits of maidenly temperance often betray themselves; self-accusatory excuses are counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jealousy and curiosity are pernicious
rubrics_metrics.description: Curiosity is vicious here; 'tis folly to examine into a disease for which there is no physic that does not inflame and make it worse; jealousy can poison life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking proof of a partner's infidelity often makes matters worse — the informer must bring remedy; discretion and avoiding needless inquiry preserve peace. Remedies for jealousy are limited (flight or patience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbidding increases desire
rubrics_metrics.description: Raising the value of the place or forbidding something enhances desire and makes pursuants more eager to attack; interdiction incites those who are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psychological insight: prohibition and excessive strictness can backfire by heightening temptation (example: Messalina's behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion about private misfortunes
rubrics_metrics.description: It is injurious to drag private misfortunes into public knowledge; the character of cuckold is indelible and publicizing private doubt only increases harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should avoid exposing private domestic troubles; social reputation and the silence of others often stand in for actual truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay and restraint as aesthetic/thrift in love
rubrics_metrics.description: To stay love's flight and delay it with preambles increases its value; small signs (a glance, a bow, a word) should stand for favour and recompense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching lovers (and women) to parcel out favours and to make desires wait heightens pleasure and prolongs reward; impatience cheapens the delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for naturalness and vigour in language
rubrics_metrics.description: Style ought to be 'nervous and solid' — not soft or languishing; language should be full of natural and continued vigour rather than forced ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer directness and force over delicate, affected rhetoric: the best expressions arise from strong, simple conception rather than clever verbal quibbles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense (conception) should produce words
rubrics_metrics.description: The sense (vivid conception) illuminates and produces the words; he who conceives simply speaks simply; language must arise from clear thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good phrasing follows from clear, deep apprehension of the subject; words should signify flesh-and-bone ideas, not airy flourishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affected novelty and meaningless new words
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not invent strange new words or adopt a new style merely for novelty; French scribblers' affectation of strange style depresses matter when they care not what words signify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New words without substantive meaning are an anti-pattern; prefer established terms when they carry more energy and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrich existing vocabulary by vigorous usage, don't fabricate
rubrics_metrics.description: Wits do not create words but enrich their own and give them weight by the uses they put them to; adapt and strain language to new services rather than inventing vocabulary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borrow from fertile domains (hunting, war) and transplant useful forms of speaking rather than contriving empty neologisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct inadvertent errors but not customary faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct accidental errors you notice, but do not betray the constant imperfections that make your work 'exactly mine'; resist altering customary idiom just to court grammatical purity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the voice and character of the writer; fix slips but not the cultural or customary turns of phrase that define personal style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write in a personal, authentic voice (own your work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal end and perfection of my work is to be exactly mine; represent yourself to the life — a book should make the world know you in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value authenticity over imitation; your writing should reflect your person and not be merely an exercise in borrowed mannerisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of imitation's hold
rubrics_metrics.description: Imitation leaves marks: whoever you steadfastly look upon easily leaves some impression upon you; vices and mannerisms especially cling and are infectious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be self-aware: imitation is powerful and often unconscious, and may produce undue affectation or deformities in style and behavior.
